correctness.rationale: Lemma 1 proves a necessary and sufficient three-white-vertex condition using maximum path degree two and a complete three-force continuation. Every exchange is uniquely assigned to a two-white-vertex common intersection. The explicit third-vertex completion table gives both cubic edge counts and exactly n^2-5n+4 nonlocal exchanges. The overlapping-fibre argument and one cross-parity slide prove connectedness for n>=7, while n=6 and n=5 are separately handled. Two standalone scripts independently replay direct forcing for n=5..12 and structural enumeration for n=5..60; these finite checks are supplementary and not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Optimal sets in dense path complements are a natural test case for physically constrained reconfiguration. The theorem identifies the sharp transition from three frozen states at order five to full slide connectivity at every higher order, with explicit constructive fibre bridges. Its cubic edge formulas and exact quadratic loss quantify the effect of locality and show the lost fraction vanishes. These statements are neither a known scalar minimum nor a numerical recomputation.
